chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Al-Fadl ibn Kathir, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no faith for the one who has no bashfulness.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between bashfulness and faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often interpreted to mean that bashfulness (hiya) serves as the protective veil for faith, preventing it from being eroded by sin or arrogance. The absence of hiya is viewed not merely as a character flaw but as a spiritual deficiency that compromises the integrity of one's belief. This concept underscores the practical manifestation of iman through moral self-restraint and humility before God.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Al Fazl Bin Kaseer, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no Emān for the one who has no ‘Hiyā’ bashfulness for him’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from al-Fadl ibn Kathir from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
One has no belief if he does not have bashfulness.’”
